145	### 3. Dirty keys: a 64-bit integer, `(KIND << 32) | id`, declared per block
146	
147	Every owner GDD already writes this encoding (Graph LS-20, Layout LY-32, Body BDY-21, Emitter EM-26). This ADR fixes it.
148	
149	| Bits | Field | Range | Notes |
150	|---|---|---|---|
151	| 63 | sign | always 0 | a key is positive |
152	| 32 to 62 | `KIND` | 1 to `0x7FFF` by rule | kind 0 is reserved (key 0 is invalid); the cap keeps every key below 2^47, exact as a `float`, and strictly below `NO_KEY` |
153	| 0 to 31 | `id` | 0 to `0xFFFFFFFF` | 0 for block-singleton families (`T`, `WEB/T`, `WEB/POD`, `ATT/L`, `ATT/P`) |
154	
155	- **The key is block-local.** `(layout.state, SEC/3)` and `(graph.state, SEC/3)` are different keys; the batch names the block. Kinds are declared per block, so two blocks may reuse a number. The shared family names in the GDDs (`S/<seam_id>`, `SEC/<id>`) are documentation, not a shared namespace.
156	- **The `ALL` sentinel is a batch flag**, not a key value (§ 5), so no key value is reserved for it.
157	- **`NO_KEY = 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`** (INT64_MAX, probed) is the empty-slot sentinel of the buffers in § 4. It can never be a valid key.
158	- **Always integers.** No `String`, `StringName`, `float` or `Variant` key is ever built (Graph LS-20: no String per key per run). Composite ids that are naturally pairs (Graph `L/<loop>/<anchor>`) are packed by the owner into the 32-bit id (for example loop in the high 16 bits and anchor in the low 16) and range-checked under `STRICT_DEBUG`.
159	- **Packed arrays holding keys are `PackedInt64Array`.** (ADR-0003 used `PackedInt32Array` for the hook schedule; a key needs 47 bits.)
160	
161	```gdscript
162	class_name DirtyKey extends RefCounted          # static helpers only, never instantiated
163	const NO_KEY: int = 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
164	const MAX_KIND: int = 0x7FFF
165	static func make(kind: int, id: int) -> int:   # STRICT_DEBUG range-checks; release trusts the caller
166		return (kind << 32) | id
167	static func kind_of(key: int) -> int:
168		return key >> 32
169	static func id_of(key: int) -> int:
170		return key & 0xFFFFFFFF
171	```
172	
173	**Key spaces are declared at `BOOTING`**, one per block, with every other descriptor field (a missing field fails boot, CR-6). This is how the debug audit and the printers know the vocabulary, and how a block says whether a write without a key is legal (§ 7).
174	
175	```gdscript
176	class_name KeySpaceDescriptor extends RefCounted
177	var block_id: StringName
178	var kind_ids: PackedInt32Array            # e.g. [1, 2, 3]
179	var kind_names: Array[StringName]         # e.g. [&"SEC", &"BODY", &"SEAM"], same order; for diagnostics only
180	var event_ids: PackedInt32Array           # event kinds this block may emit (may be empty)
181	var event_names: Array[StringName]
182	var quiet_writes_allowed: bool            # true: a write that changes the block may legitimately mark no key (quantised families)
183	# BlockRegistrar (ADR-0003) gains:  func register_key_space(desc: KeySpaceDescriptor) -> void
184	```
185	
186	MVP families named by the GDDs (the numeric kind of a family the GDD did not number is the owner's ADR to fix; only distinctness inside a block is required here):
187	
188	| Block | Families | Kinds fixed by the GDD |
189	|---|---|---|
190	| `graph.state` | `C/<cid>`, `B/<cid>`, `N/<id>`, `F/<id>`, `L/<loop>/<anchor>`, `S/<seam_id>`, `T`, `SEC/<id>` | COMP 1, BAND 2, NODE 3, EDGE 4, DESC 5, LOOP 6, SEAM 7, TOPO 8, SECTION 9 (LS-20) |
191	| `layout.state` | `SEC/<section_id>`, `BODY/<body_id>`, `S/<seam_id>` | SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3 (LY-32) |
192	| `body.state` | `BODY/<body_id>`, `ACT/<actor_id>` | BODY 2, ACT 4 (BDY-21) |
193	| `emitter.state` | `E/<emitter id>` | owner |
194	| `suit.state` | `S/<PlayerId>` | owner |
195	| `web.state` | `WEB/<derelict_id>`, `WEB/T`, `WEB/POD` | owner |
196	| `attention.state` | `ATT/L`, `ATT/P` | owner |
197	
198	**`MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`** (kernel knob, 256, range 32 to 4096, at least 128 while `graph.state` is registered). Buffers are sized from the value at the registry freeze. The knob may be **lowered** at run time (it takes effect at the next tick's P0, KRN AC: a change during P2 of T uses the old value in T's P5); raising it above the sized capacity is refused with the existing `KNOB_REFUSED` violation. This keeps the buffers fixed-size for the whole run.
199	
200	### 4. Collection in the write scope: a fixed `PackedInt64Array` per block, `has()` dedupe, exact collapse
201	
202	The GDD criteria require deduplication (marks `a, b, b` give `{a, b}`; writing a key to its existing value still marks) and a collapse on the **distinct** count. A `Dictionary` used as a set allocates on growth and would be iterated; a GDScript linear scan costs up to 256 element reads per mark. A preallocated native-scanned array does neither.
203	
204	```gdscript
205	class_name KeyBuf extends RefCounted             # kernel-internal; one per block for the tick, one per block for the frame
206	var buf: PackedInt64Array                        # size = capacity (the sized MAX_DIRTY_KEYS); filled with NO_KEY; never resized
207	var count: int                                   # distinct keys held (valid while not is_all)
208	var is_all: bool                                 # true once a distinct key arrived with count == capacity
209	func mark(key: int) -> void:
210		if is_all or buf.has(key):                   # native scan; capacity <= 4096
211			return
212		if count == buf.size():
213			is_all = true                            # the 257th distinct key at capacity 256: collapse, drop keys
214			count = 0
215			return
216		buf[count] = key
217		count += 1
218	func close() -> void:                            # at P4: native sort puts NO_KEY at the tail; keys are ascending, unique
219		if not is_all and count > 1: buf.sort()
220	func clear() -> void:
221		buf.fill(NO_KEY); count = 0; is_all = false
222	```
223	
224	- **`scope.mark_dirty(block_id, key)`** (ADR-0003 § 4 signature, unchanged) does, in order: (1) if the scope is not currently open for `block_id` (no successful `open_for` for that block in this scope use) it writes nothing and counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` (not counted again once the scope has faulted); (2) if `key <= 0` or `key >= NO_KEY` it counts `DIRTY_KEY_INVALID` and returns (always on: two compares); (3) in `INIT` and `RESTORE` phases it returns (those keys are discarded, ADR-0003 § 4; § 6 delivers `ALL` instead); (4) under `STRICT_DEBUG` it checks the key's kind against the block's key space and counts `DIRTY_KEY_KIND_UNDECLARED`; (5) `tick_buf[block].mark(key)`.
225	- **Resolving `block_id` to a block index** is one typed `Dictionary[StringName, int]` lookup, built at the freeze and read-only afterwards (the kernel reads it by key, never iterates it). `open_for` caches the index in the scope so `mark_dirty` for the block just opened does not look it up again.
226	- **A mark is not a diff.** A key marked for a write of an unchanged value is delivered (KRN AC). Over-marking is legal; under-marking is a defect (§ 7).
227	- **Exactness.** Capacity is the knob value, so exactly 256 distinct keys are listed and the 257th gives `ALL`; a key marked 1,000 times is one key (probed 2026-10-28, `EXACT256`: `is_all` false, count 256; `OVERFLOW` at 257: `is_all` true).
228	- **Dirty-block bookkeeping.** The kernel keeps one flag per block (a `PackedByteArray` of `MAX_BLOCKS` 128) set on the first mark or event of a tick; P4 scans it in ascending block index, so block order is deterministic and a quiet tick costs one scan of at most 128 bytes.
229	- **No setter, no automatic tracking.** Marks come only from the mutator (registry `write_outside_writescope_or_setter_dirty`).
230	
231	### 5. Types: `ChangeBatch`, `NotifyEvent`, `DirtyAccumulator`
232	
233	**`ChangeBatch`** is a reused facade over the kernel's closed buffer. It is not a copy and not a container the subscriber may keep.
234	
235	```gdscript
236	class_name ChangeBatch extends RefCounted
237	var block_id: StringName
238	var tick: int                          # the last committed tick this batch covers
239	var first_tick: int                    # equals tick for PER_TICK batches; first tick of the frame for merged batches
240	var is_all: bool                       # true: re-read everything you use from this block; count is 0
241	var count: int                         # number of distinct keys (0 when is_all)
242	var event_count: int
243	func key(i: int) -> int                # 0 <= i < count; keys are ascending and unique
244	func has(key: int) -> bool             # bsearch over the sorted buffer
245	func event(i: int) -> NotifyEvent      # emission order; ticks ascending in a merged batch
246	```
247	
248	- **The container type of `change_keys` is the kernel-held `PackedInt64Array` behind `key(i)` / `has(key)`.** The array itself is never handed out (packed arrays pass by reference and cannot be made read-only, ADR-0007 review B2).
249	- **Valid only during the handler call.** One `ChangeBatch` object exists per block per cadence and is re-armed for every delivery; under `STRICT_DEBUG` it is poisoned (`tick = -1`) after the call so a retained reference fails visibly. A subscriber copies what it needs, normally into a `DirtyAccumulator`.
250	- **Order.** Keys ascending and unique (canonical, so HOST and MIRROR batches compare equal and tests compare arrays). Subscribers must still treat the batch as a set.
251	- **`is_all`** replaces the old `ALL` sentinel. A block with no keys and no events produces no batch at all.
252	
253	**`DirtyAccumulator`** is the subscriber-side union that Failure & Trail FT-15 and every PRESENTATION system needs: store the keys since the last render callback, collapse on overflow, expose `has`.
254	
255	```gdscript
256	class_name DirtyAccumulator extends RefCounted
257	func _init(capacity: int) -> void              # facet.key_capacity
258	var is_all: bool
259	var count: int
260	func absorb(batch: ChangeBatch) -> void        # is_all if batch.is_all or the union would exceed capacity; otherwise has()-union
261	func has(key: int) -> bool                     # true for every key while is_all
262	func key(i: int) -> int
263	func clear() -> void                           # call in the render callback after consuming
264	```
265	
266	It uses the same `KeyBuf` code as § 4 and allocates nothing after `_init`.
267	
268	**`NotifyEvent`** (P5 events: `BODY_TRANSFER_WELD`, `BODY_TRANSFER_DETACH`, `BODY_TRANSFER_POD`, `BODY_DOCK_CONTACT`, `BODY_HULL_SEPARATION`, `POD_DEPARTED`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`, `DERELICT_UNLOADED`, `BERTHED`, `UNBERTHED`, `FIRST_BOARDED`). An event is a kind and up to six integers, never state:
269	
270	```gdscript
271	class_name NotifyEvent extends RefCounted      # pooled; the kernel preallocates MAX_EVENTS_PER_FRAME
272	var kind: int                                  # declared in the emitting block's KeySpaceDescriptor.event_ids
273	var tick: int
274	var a0: int; var a1: int; var a2: int; var a3: int; var a4: int; var a5: int
275	# WriteScope (ADR-0003) gains:
276	# func emit_event(block_id: StringName, kind: int, a0: int = 0, a1: int = 0, a2: int = 0, a3: int = 0, a4: int = 0, a5: int = 0) -> void
277	```
278	
279	- The GDD payloads fit: `BODY_TRANSFER{weld | detach | pod}` is three kinds with `{actor_id, seat, old_body, new_body, frame_delta_px.x, frame_delta_px.y}` (six ints, the sub-kind folded into the event kind); `POD_DEPARTED` is five ints; the tick travels in the event, not the args.
280	- **An event belongs to the block that emitted it** and is delivered in that block's batch to every subscription on that block, any class (a batch may therefore have events and no keys). It is not a second channel and needs no second subscription.
281	- `emit_event` follows the same scope rules as `mark_dirty` (open block required; discarded in `INIT`, `RESTORE`, `CLOSED`). The pool holds `MAX_EVENTS_PER_TICK` (64) per tick and `MAX_EVENTS_PER_FRAME` (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` x 64) per frame; overflow drops the newest and counts `EVENT_OVERFLOW`. Events are **not** unioned: a merged batch carries every event of every committed tick of the frame, in order. The pool is preallocated, so an event tick allocates nothing in the kernel either (the call's integer arguments are evaluated at the call site only).
282	
283	### 6. Delivery: per tick, catch-up merge, early exit, restore
284	
285	Each block has two `KeyBuf`s (tick and frame) and an event list for each.
286	
287	**P4 close.** After `commit_baseline`, for each dirty block in ascending index: `tick_buf.close()`. If the tick **faulted**, every tick buffer and event list is cleared and nothing is delivered or merged for it (KRN-NOT-01: a faulting tick contributes nothing; P4 never ran).
288	
289	**P5, per tick.** The kernel applies deferred subscription changes, then for each dirty block in ascending index and each `PER_TICK` subscription of that block in subscription order, arms the shared `NotifyContext`, calls the handler with the block's tick batch, checks the returned token (identity and epoch, ADR-0003 § 3), and records `INCOMPLETE` or `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER` as needed. Then each tick buffer is folded into its frame buffer: if the frame buffer is empty the two `KeyBuf` objects are swapped (O(1)); otherwise the keys are unioned with `has`, and a union beyond capacity sets `is_all`; events are appended. The tick buffer is cleared. The result-buffer flush follows the change batch, as in the kernel GDD.
290	
291	**Frame end.** `TickDriver.frame` calls `Kernel.deliver_frame_end()` as its **last step, on every exit path**, after the result flush and the paused service cycle (ADR-0001 gains this step, see Cross-ADR amendments). The kernel applies deferred subscription changes and delivers each dirty frame buffer, in ascending block index, to the block's `FRAME_MERGED` subscriptions with `tick` = the last committed tick and `first_tick` = the first; then clears the frame buffers. A one-tick frame (the common case) therefore costs one swap and one delivery per block, not a union. A zero-tick frame delivers nothing.
292	
293	- **Early exit** (a P6 pause, a restore request, a fault): the loop stops, the frame buffer already holds only committed ticks, and `deliver_frame_end()` delivers it after the state change is visible to the driver (KRN-NOT-01: pause at tick 3 of 4 gives the union of ticks 1 to 3 with `tick == 3`; a fault at tick 2 gives tick 1 only).
294	- **Paused service cycle** (P1, P2, P4, P5, P6, no P3, `T` unchanged, once per rendered frame while `PAUSED`): its P4 and P5 follow the same rules with `tick = T`; its marks come from `PAUSED_APPLY` scopes and reach `PER_TICK` classes immediately and merged classes at that frame's `deliver_frame_end()`.
295	- **Restore and new game.** ADR-0003 discards keys marked in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes. On the transition `LOADING -> RUNNING` the kernel calls `deliver_all()`: it first clears every tick buffer, frame buffer and event list (the world was replaced; any pending merged union is superseded), then delivers **one `ALL` batch per registered block to every subscription of every class**, with `tick` = the restored `T`, before the first tick of the run. This is the GDD's "one `ALL`, then silence"; owners seed their quantised last-emitted buckets in `post_restore` so no key follows (Graph LS-20, Suit SE-34). Events emitted during `INIT` and `RESTORE` are discarded.
296	- **`SAVING`** delivers nothing (snapshot is a read). **`FAULTED`** delivers only what `deliver_frame_end()` still holds from committed ticks; blocks half-applied by the fault are visible through read views without a notification, which is acceptable because the fault screen replaces the play view.
297	- **Batches for a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block** follow the same delivery; which subscribers may be attached to a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block is ADR-0009 and ADR-0024's rule, enforced there.
298	
299	### 7. The missed-mark audit and the touch serial
300	
301	The architecture calls for "a debug-build check that every changed block marked a dirty key". A literal check is wrong for blocks whose GDD forbids a key per write: the Graph fires a key only when a quantum bucket changes (LS-20), the Emitter's pose never dirties (EM-26), Web Map marks zero keys per tick during a leg (WM-2). So the audit is built on two separate facts.
302	
303	**The touch serial (always on, also in release).** The kernel keeps `touch_serial[block]`, a `PackedInt64Array` of `MAX_BLOCKS`. Every successful `scope.open_for(block)` stores the scope's serial into the block's slot (one store; the serial is a kernel counter incremented at each scope arming, so it also advances for same-`T` paused cycles). Because every mutator begins with `open_for` (ADR-0003), "this block may have changed" is derived by the kernel without the owner's help and is independent of whether the owner marked a presentation key. This ADR **exposes** the serial (`Kernel.touch_serial(block_index)`) and **recommends** it to ADR-0005 as the invalidation input of the per-block hash cache, because a dirty key cannot serve: a quantised Graph write that crosses no bucket changes the hash and marks no key. The decision belongs to ADR-0005; the kernel GDD D.12 already says the cache is "invalidated by the block's dirty bit (any write in P2/P3 clears it)" and is used "for the diagnostics cadence only" (every determinism check hashes uncached), so the risk of leaving it on keys is a stale diagnostics value, not a wrong replay verdict. The serial is a registry member under the H1 allow-list.
304	
305	**The audit (dev, playtest and test builds only).** It reuses the per-block hash the `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` already takes just before P5 (ADR-0003 § 7); it adds no hash pass. The hash is ADR-0005's `block_hash(block_id, uncached = true)` over the owner's `snapshot`. A sweep compares each audited block with its previous sweep and applies one rule:
306	
307	> **`MISSED_DIRTY_MARK`**: the block's hash changed since the previous sweep, `touch_serial` advanced (the block was opened), **no key was marked and no `ALL` was set** in that interval, and the block's key space has `quiet_writes_allowed == false`.
308	
309	- A block that changed with the serial **not** advanced is a write outside a scope or a leaked mutable reference; that is the existing `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` and is not duplicated here.
310	- A key marked for an unchanged value is not a violation (marked, not diffed).
311	- **Cadence.** In unit, integration and CI soak tests with small worlds the sweep runs **every tick** (`AUDIT_EVERY_TICK`); in dev and playtest builds it runs at the tripwire's `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` (60) and within `TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` (1.0), so there it is a sample, not a proof. A bool guards the whole path; release exports pay one branch per tick.
312	- **Quiet blocks** (`quiet_writes_allowed == true`: Graph, Emitter, Body, Suit, Controller, Sanity, any block with a continuous family) are not audited by the hash rule, because it cannot distinguish a forgotten bucket-crossing mark from a legal sub-quantum write. For them the guarantee is the per-mutator test of Implementation Guidelines (a fixture runs each mutator in a fresh kernel and asserts that its discrete changes mark a declared kind), plus a per-block diagnostics counter `QUIET_WRITE_TICKS` (ticks on which the block was touched with zero keys), shown in the Debug Overlay so a block that never marks anything is visible.
313	- **Scope of coverage.** The audit hashes only blocks `block_hash` supports (`persist` blocks, kernel GDD). A derived `persist == false` block is covered by its mutator tests alone (Open Question).
314	- **What it cannot see.** A mutator that marks the wrong key of a declared kind. The mutator test asserts the specific keys.
315	- **Release.** Nothing detects a missed mark at run time in a release export; the consequence is a stale display until the next full reconcile (Lighting LO-3 reconciles every `FULL_RECONCILE_TICKS` 60). This is accepted and recorded.
316	
317	New violation names (counters; each also calls `violation_handler` under `STRICT_DEBUG`): `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED`, `DIRTY_KEY_INVALID`, `DIRTY_KEY_KIND_UNDECLARED`, `EVENT_OVERFLOW`, `MISSED_DIRTY_MARK`. They extend ADR-0003's closed violation set, which omitted `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` although the kernel GDD already requires it.
318

354	### Implementation Guidelines
355	- **Must** deliver change notification only through the kernel registry (`subscribe`); **must never** declare an engine `signal` for kernel changes, `connect` to a kernel object, or use `Signal.emit` to notify a subscriber from `src/kernel/`.
356	- **Must** register a `KeySpaceDescriptor` for every block, with `quiet_writes_allowed` stated explicitly; **must never** mint a key of an undeclared kind.
357	- **Must** build keys with `(kind << 32) | id` from integers (`DirtyKey.make` or the same expression); **must never** build a key from a `String`, `StringName`, `float` or `Variant`, or let an `id` exceed 32 bits.
358	- **Must** mark dirty keys only with `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator that changed the data, after `scope.open_for`; **must never** mark from a property setter, from a hook that did not open the block, or outside a scope.
359	- **Must** mark a key on every discrete change a subscriber could need to wake for (create, remove, structural change, bucket crossing); **may** skip a key for a sub-quantum write only if the block's key space declares `quiet_writes_allowed`.
360	- **Must** emit P5 events only through `scope.emit_event` with integer arguments; **must never** put a state value, `String`, `Vector2i` or `Dictionary` in an event.
361	- **Must** give every mutator a unit test that runs it in a fresh kernel fixture and asserts the exact keys it marks (the fixture subscribes a `RecordingSubscriber` and compares the batch); **must** keep `AUDIT_EVERY_TICK` on in every integration and soak test.
362	- **Must** write subscriber handlers as `(batch, ctx) -> CompletionToken` method Callables on long-lived objects, ending `return ctx.complete()`; **must never** pass a lambda or a `.bind()` result, retain a `ChangeBatch` past the handler, hold or duplicate the kernel's buffer, or call a mutator, `submit` or a scope from a handler.
363	- **Must** accumulate into a `DirtyAccumulator` and clear it in the render callback after use; **must** treat `is_all` as "re-read everything you use from this block".
364	- **Must** make a block or hook owner's own methods unsubscribed; if an owner needs presentation-like output it creates a separate object that subscribes (CR-10).
365	- **Must** call `Kernel.deliver_frame_end()` as the last step of `TickDriver.frame`, including for a zero-tick frame, an early exit and a paused frame; **must never** deliver a merged class from P5.
366	- **Must** treat `touch_serial` as the kernel's "this block may have changed" fact (set only by a granted `open_for`); **should** use it, not dirty keys, wherever a cache must be invalidated by "any write" (ADR-0005 decides for the hash cache).
367	- **Must never** allocate in `mark_dirty`, `emit_event`, P4 close, a quiet-tick P5 or `deliver_frame_end`; the verification is the `OBJECT_COUNT` plus identity checks of Validation Criteria.
368	- **Must** keep the audit behind one dev-or-test bool; **must never** let it run a hash pass of its own beyond the tripwire's.

370	## Alternatives Considered
371	
372	### Alternative 1: Engine signals for notification
373	- **Description**: The kernel declares a `changed(batch)` signal (or one per block); subscribers `connect` method Callables; P5 emits.
374	- **Pros**: The idiomatic Godot mechanism; the engine disconnects freed receivers; cost equals a `Callable.call` loop (probed 157 versus 155 ns per call at 10 subscribers).
375	- **Cons**: No return value, so the completion-token contract and per-subscriber `INCOMPLETE` cannot exist; no class and no cadence selection; no per-block filter, so every handler is called for every block; silent disconnect hides `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER`; the CR-10 snapshot behaviour and subscribe-time checks have nowhere to live; emission order is the engine's (training knowledge, not relied on).
376	- **Rejection Reason**: Semantic fit, not cost. The kernel GDD's lean is confirmed (OQ-4), gated on KRN-LAT-02.
377	
378	### Alternative 2: A `Dictionary` per block as the dirty set
379	- **Description**: `dirty[block][key] = true`; deliver `dirty[block].keys()`.
380	- **Pros**: Deduplication for free; short code.
381	- **Cons**: Allocation on growth and `keys()` allocates a fresh `Array` every delivery (fails KRN-PERF-01's zero-container quiet tick and the active-tick budget); iteration order is not a contract the kernel wants to lean on (CR-13); every key is a boxed `Variant`.
382	- **Rejection Reason**: Allocation and order. The fixed `PackedInt64Array` with `has` gives the same semantics with neither.
383	
384	### Alternative 3: String-keyed families (`"C/12"`)
385	- **Description**: Keys are strings built per mark, as the Graph GDD's "SD alternative" would have.
386	- **Pros**: Readable in logs; no encoding to learn.
387	- **Cons**: A `String` is built per key per run (the Graph's reason for choosing integers at VS-A, ADR-LSG-06); string compares in `has`; collisions between families need prefix discipline.
388	- **Rejection Reason**: Allocation at the Graph's volume. Names are recovered from the key space for diagnostics instead.
389	
390	### Alternative 4: Automatic dirty tracking (setters, or a hash diff after each mutator)
391	- **Description**: Property setters mark a block dirty, or the kernel hashes a block before and after every mutator and marks it if different.
392	- **Pros**: Owners cannot forget a mark.
393	- **Cons**: 4.7 packed-array element writes call no setter (probed), and the Graph, Layout, Body and Emitter write element-wise; a diff needs a hash per mutator call (CR-12's tripwire is budgeted at two per batch, not one per call) and contradicts "marked, not diffed" for an unchanged write; neither produces a key, only a block-level change, which is the `ALL` cost the key scheme exists to avoid.
394	- **Rejection Reason**: Cannot work on 4.7 and cannot name what changed.
395	
396	### Alternative 5: Deliver every tick to every class, no catch-up merge
397	- **Description**: PRESENTATION also gets each tick's batch in a catch-up frame.
398	- **Pros**: Simplest semantics.
399	- **Cons**: A four-tick frame pays P5 four times for a reader that only ever draws the last committed state; ratified against in R-12.
400	- **Rejection Reason**: Ruled out by the user (R-12). Per-tick delivery stays for INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION.
401	
402	### Alternative 6: An open-addressed hash set instead of `has()` scanning
403	- **Description**: Per block, a power-of-two `PackedInt64Array` table with linear probing plus an insertion list; `mark` is O(1) expected.
404	- **Pros**: Constant-time marks regardless of capacity; matters if `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` is raised toward 4096.
405	- **Cons**: More code, a hash that must avoid 64-bit overflow, a larger table to clear; at the default 256 the scan costs 160 to 230 ns per mark (probed), and a worst-case 256-distinct tick 52 us, well under the proposal.
406	- **Rejection Reason**: Not needed at 256. **Kept as the documented fallback** if KRN-LAT-02 shows the `has()` scan is a problem on a release export; the `KeyBuf` interface does not change.
407	
408	### Alternative 7: Block-less `subscribe(class, handler)` receiving every block
409	- **Description**: The architecture sketch's two-argument form; each handler filters by `batch.block_id`.
410	- **Pros**: Fewer registrations.
411	- **Cons**: A subscriber that cares about two blocks is called for up to 128; the cost scales with subscribers times dirty blocks; Layout LY-32 already assumes per-block subscription.
412	- **Rejection Reason**: Wasted calls; the wildcard survives for `DIAGNOSTIC` only.
413	
414	### Alternative 8: Copy the subscriber list at the start of every P5
415	- **Description**: The literal CR-10 snapshot.
416	- **Pros**: Obviously correct.
417	- **Cons**: One array allocation per tick for a list that almost never changes.
418	- **Rejection Reason**: Deferred application gives identical observable behaviour with no per-tick allocation (§ 2).
419	
420	### Alternative 9: A `HOST_SERVICE` subscriber class for Save/Load
421	- **Description**: A sixth class for host services that need events (autosave triggers).
422	- **Pros**: Matches how Save/Load actually consumes `POD_ARRIVED` and `BERTHED`.
423	- **Cons**: CR-10's table is closed; the architecture already has Save/Load poll owner read views (`last_shape_change_T`, `last_salvage_T`).
424	- **Rejection Reason**: Not decided here; recorded as an Open Question. The recommended path is polling a read view.
425	
426	## Consequences
427	
428	### Positive
429	- One notification path with the token contract, the two cadences, the owner rule and the lifetime rules in one place, testable with stub subscribers and no scene.
430	- Marking is a native scan of a fixed array: no allocation, exact collapse, canonical sorted batches.
431	- `ALL` is a flag, so no key value is reserved and the accumulator logic is one union function every presentation system shares.
432	- The touch serial offers ADR-0005 a sound invalidation signal even for quantised blocks, decoupled from presentation keys.
433	- Events share the block's batch, so audio and autosave triggers need no second subscription and survive a catch-up frame.
434	- A forgotten mark is caught in every integration test for non-quiet blocks, and every mutator has a test that names its keys.
435	
436	### Negative
437	- Every presentation handler is `(batch, ctx) -> CompletionToken`, not the one-argument `void` of the architecture sketch.
438	- Manual marking remains a discipline; quiet blocks (the largest ones) get a test-level guarantee, not a runtime one, and a wrong key of a declared kind is invisible to the audit.
439	- The mark cost is O(capacity) per distinct key (native scan); raising `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` toward 4096 makes the fallback of Alternative 6 necessary.
440	- `TickDriver.frame` gains a step and ADR-0003 gains `emit_event`, `register_key_space` and five violation names; both sibling ADRs must be amended in the same pass.
441	- A block must declare its key space even if it never marks a key.
442	- Release builds detect no missed marks.
443	
444	## Risks
445	- **A mutator forgets `scope.mark_dirty` on a quiet block.** The audit cannot see it. Mitigation: the per-mutator test with exact keys, `QUIET_WRITE_TICKS` in the overlay, Lighting's `FULL_RECONCILE_TICKS`, and review against the key space table.
446	- **`has()` is slower than probed on a release template.** Mitigation: KRN-LAT-02 measures the 256-distinct worst case; Alternative 6 is the drop-in.

484	## Performance Implications
485	- **CPU.** All figures are **proposals pending KRN-LAT-02 on a release export (RM-DESKTOP, RM-DECK)**; the kernel GDD defines `t_P5` but no budget. Proposed: **P5 plus frame-end delivery <= 0.25 ms P99** on the stress workload (12 dirty blocks, 40 subscriptions, a 38-key Graph cascade, four events), inside the 4.0 ms one-tick simulation frame. Indicative editor-build costs (probed): 160 to 230 ns per mark including amortised sort and clear (38 distinct keys: 8.8 us per tick; the 256-distinct worst case: 52 us per tick); about 160 ns per `Callable.call` plus context re-arm per delivery; a quiet tick is one scan of at most 128 flag bytes and zero calls. A one-tick frame swaps buffers instead of unioning.
486	- **Memory.** Two `KeyBuf`s per block at 256 keys of 8 bytes: 4 KiB per block, 128 KiB for 32 blocks (512 KiB for 128 blocks, the `MAX_BLOCKS` ceiling). One `ChangeBatch` per block per cadence; the event pool (64 x `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` `NotifyEvent`s); at most 96 subscriptions. The registry and pools are allocated once at the freeze.
487	- **Load Time.** Buffer and pool allocation at the freeze; `deliver_all` once per load, one handler call per subscription.
488	- **Network.** None at MVP. REPLICATION receives per-tick batches in VS-B (ADR-0032); keys carry no state, so the replication shape does not change the encoding.

498	## Validation Criteria
499	- **KRN-LAT-02 (gates acceptance for cost).** On a release export of the headless kernel skeleton, P5 plus frame-end delivery meets the proposal on the stress workload; the 256-distinct `has()` worst case and the registry-versus-signal baseline are recorded (the baseline is information only).
500	- Marks `a, b, b` in one tick give one batch `(B, T, {a, b})`; a block with no marks produces none; a write of an unchanged value still lists its key; the batch carries only `block_id`, ticks, keys and events.
501	- Exactly 256 distinct keys are listed and sibling block `C` with 3 keys is unaffected; 257 give `is_all` for `B` only; the same key marked 1,000 times is one key.
502	- A `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` change during P2 of tick `T` leaves `T`'s P5 on the old value and `T+1` on the new; a raise above the sized capacity is `KNOB_REFUSED`.
503	- A four-tick catch-up frame in which `B` marks `a` in tick 1 and `b` in tick 3 delivers one batch `(B, T_last, {a, b})` with `first_tick` 1 to a PRESENTATION subscriber, four batches to an INPUT_SURFACE subscriber, and two blocks of 200 distinct keys each in different ticks merge to `is_all`. Events of all four ticks arrive, in order, in the merged batch.
504	- KRN-NOT-01: a pause at tick 3 of 4 gives the union of ticks 1 to 3 with `tick == 3`; a fault at tick 2 gives tick 1's keys only; a frame ending in a restore delivers `ALL` for every block to every class after the kernel is `RUNNING`, and no pending merged union survives it.
505	- KRN-NOT-02: a freed subscriber is pruned, `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER` +1, no engine error, no `INCOMPLETE`; `unsubscribe()` stops delivery; a handler that unsubscribes a peer during P5 leaves the peer receiving this batch and none after; a handler that subscribes affects the next boundary only.
506	- KRN-NOT-03: after `dispose()` twice, registries are empty and the kernel's instance count (by `weakref`) is 0.
507	- Subscribe refusals each count `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` and fault nothing: a lambda, a `.bind()` result, an invalid Callable, a wrong arity, a block or hook owner's own method (while a separate input-adapter object of the same system is accepted), `DIAGNOSTIC` without the dev predicate, `REPLICATION` at MVP, an unknown block after the freeze, the 97th subscription; an unknown block before the freeze fails boot with `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY`.
508	- A handler that returns something other than the armed token is `INCOMPLETE` against its name while the other subscribers receive the batch and the kernel stays `RUNNING`; a handler that calls a mutator writes nothing and counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` once.
509	- KRN-PERF-01: a quiet tick with 32 blocks and 10 subscriptions performs zero calls, zero kernel container allocations; **zero allocation is tested two ways** (as in ADR-0007, because `OBJECT_COUNT` misses arrays): `OBJECT_COUNT` is flat over 600 ticks that mark, deliver and clear, and the same `ChangeBatch` and `NotifyEvent` objects (`is_same`) are returned on consecutive ticks.
510	- Keys: `DirtyKey.make(kind, id)` round-trips through `kind_of` and `id_of` for kind 1 and `0x7FFF` and id 0 and `0xFFFFFFFF`; a key of 0, a negative key and `NO_KEY` are refused with `DIRTY_KEY_INVALID`; an undeclared kind under `STRICT_DEBUG` is `DIRTY_KEY_KIND_UNDECLARED`.
511	- `mark_dirty` and `emit_event` in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes record the touch serial and discard keys and events; a new game delivers exactly one `ALL` per block and nothing else on `LOADING -> RUNNING`.
512	- Events: 64 per tick are delivered, the 65th is dropped with `EVENT_OVERFLOW`; an event with no key makes a batch with `count` 0 and `event_count` 1.
513	- Audit: a fixture mutator on a non-quiet block that changes data and marks nothing yields `MISSED_DIRTY_MARK` with `AUDIT_EVERY_TICK`; the same mutator on a `quiet_writes_allowed` block does not; a write of an unchanged value does not; a fixture that changes a block without `open_for` is the tripwire's, not `MISSED_DIRTY_MARK`; the audit performs no hash pass beyond the tripwire's.
514	- `touch_serial` advances for every `open_for` grant, including a same-`T` paused cycle, and does not advance for a refused `open_for`.
515	- Each registered block's key space is consistent with the GDD tables of § 3 (a CI test per owner).

542	2. **Sim-side event consumers.** WM-31 lists Attention and Horror as consumers of Web Map events; CR-10 forbids block and hook owners from subscribing. 331:**5.3 Reads.** `block_hash(block_id, uncached = true) -> BlockHashResult` (D.12) is available in every build. It is a pure read: the kernel calls the owner's `snapshot` with a dedicated `SnapshotContext` of its own, encodes, hashes, and mutates no block. Order of checks: (1) unknown id or a non-`persist` block: `ok = false`, `BLOCK_HASH_UNKNOWN`, never a hash of 0; (2) the active `WriteScope` has opened the block (`scope.has_opened(block_index)`, true from the first `open_for` of that block until the scope is re-armed): `ok = false`, `BLOCK_HASH_IN_WRITE`; (3) `uncached = false` and `valid`: return the cache; (4) otherwise `snapshot`, encode, `H64`, set `ok`; an encoder error gives `BLOCK_HASH_ENCODE_ERROR`. Only a **cached** read stores into the cache (it records the current `touch_serial` with the hash, and counts one encode if it had to compute); an **uncached** read ignores the cache, writes nothing, and counts exactly one `canonical_bytes` encode. A hook that has written Layout and then reads `layout_hash()` inside the same hook therefore gets `BLOCK_HASH_IN_WRITE`: read it from another hook or a boundary, or after the writing hook returns. `snapshot` is not re-entrant (ADR-0003), so `block_hash` called from inside a `snapshot` is a defect that the context's re-entrancy flag reports.
333:**5.4 Which path uses the cache.** Only the **diagnostics cadence** (the Overlay's `state_hash` display and its HASH_DRIFT block naming) and a caller memoising its own reads may use `uncached = false`. **Every determinism check uses `uncached = true`**: G3, G4, the K-4 window, the cross-process test, the `STRICT_DEBUG` tripwire, the snapshot capture, the weld property test and the golden comparisons. It costs one extra encode per valid block per cadence in debug only. Release builds do not run it.
337:**5.6 Cost accounting.** Counters (diagnostics, never hashed, reset at BOOTING and at restore): `enc_blocks` (encodes performed), `enc_bytes`, `enc_elem_loops` (element-loop iterations over non-packed scalars), `hash_calls`, `cache_hits`, `HASH_CACHE_STALE`. KRN-PERF-01: a quiet tick with no dirty block and no reader shows `enc_blocks` = 0. KRN-PERF-02: a cached-profile read after a tick that touched `k` blocks (opened them for writing) shows `enc_blocks` = `k`, the blocks whose touch serial moved since the previous cached read; a block that was written has been opened, so `k` is the count of written blocks plus any opened and left unchanged. KRN-PERF-05: packed arrays reach the buffer by `to_byte_array()` and contribute 0 to `enc_elem_loops`. `HashingContext` over 150 KB must stay at or below 1 ms on RM-DECK (TR-lsg-037, S0-d); if a release-export measurement exceeds it, the ladder is: keep the cache (already), then hash on the Save/Load worker from the encoded bytes (the worker may call `HashingContext`), then split large packed arrays into per-section sub-payloads whose hashes fold, under a new `hash_algo`.

333:**5.4 Which path uses the cache.** Only the **diagnostics cadence** (the Overlay's `state_hash` display and its HASH_DRIFT block naming) and a caller memoising its own reads may use `uncached = false`. **Every determinism check uses `uncached = true`**: G3, G4, the K-4 window, the cross-process test, the `STRICT_DEBUG` tripwire, the snapshot capture, the weld property test and the golden comparisons. The reason is the same as D.12's: a cached comparison would pass falsely on the missed-dirty-mark bug.
335:**5.5 Stale-cache detector (hash side of ADR-0004's audit).** In `STRICT_DEBUG` and test builds, each diagnostics-cadence refresh recomputes `uncached` for every block whose cache is valid and, if the two differ, counts `HASH_CACHE_STALE`, reports a violation naming the block, and invalidates the entry. With the serial rule this fires only for a write outside a `WriteScope` or a leaked mutable reference into a block, which is the failure `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` hunts; it is cheap corroboration, not a replacement for ADR-0004's `MISSED_DIRTY_MARK` audit (which concerns presentation keys). It costs one extra encode per valid block per cadence in debug only. Release builds do not run it.
422:Added to existing contracts (assumptions on siblings, also under Related): `ModuleFacet.rng: RngFacet` (ADR-0001 / ADR-0003); `WriteScope.has_opened(block_index: int) -> bool` (ADR-0003); `Kernel.touch_serial(block_index: int) -> int` (ADR-0004 § 7, already specified there); `IntMath.ceil_div`, `lsr`, `low32` and the `b <= 0` guard on `floor_div` / `ceil_div` / `posmod_i` (ADR-0010 § 5.4 lists only `trunc_div`, `floor_div`, `posmod_i`); `det_rng_float.gd` on `float_allowlist.json` (ADR-0010 § 5.5).
517:- **A block is written outside a `WriteScope`** (or through a leaked mutable reference), so the touch serial does not advance and the cache goes stale. Mitigation: every verification path is uncached; `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE`; the debug detector (§ 5.5) names the block; the weld property test. A forgotten `mark_dirty` no longer stales the hash cache (the serial rides `open_for`); it is ADR-0004's `MISSED_DIRTY_MARK` concern.
522:- **Cross-ADR drift** (ADR-0004's mark path, ADR-0003's `has_opened`, ADR-0006's use of `hash_algo` and `block_state_hash`). Mitigation: each assumption is listed under Related and must be confirmed at the joint review.
620:  - ADR-0001 / ADR-0003: `ModuleFacet` gains `rng: RngFacet`; `kernel.clock` carries `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)` with `world_seed` set before `INIT`; `WriteScope` exposes `has_opened(block_index)`; the snapshot callable may be invoked by the kernel outside `SAVING` with a dedicated context; no new domain-0 fault codes are needed.
634:10. **Reusing the previous capture for an untouched block.** ADR-0006 rung 1 would skip `snapshot()` for a block whose cached hash is unchanged since the last capture. With the touch serial that is sound against everything except a write outside a scope (guarded by the tripwire), but it would make capture trust the serial instead of re-encoding. This ADR keeps capture, K-4 and every test uncached; adopting rung 1 is a technical-director decision made on SAVE-WRK-1's hitch measurement, and the cache exposes `entry_valid(block_index)` for it.
643:  - Cross-ADR amendments: none were stated for this ADR in the review input, so the assumptions listed under Related stay as written and remain to be confirmed at the next joint review. ADR-0004's touch serial (the fallback in the Ordering Note), ADR-0006's use of `hash_algo` and `block_state_hash`, ADR-0003's `has_opened` and ADR-0010's `src/shared/det/` placement are the assumptions most worth re-checking.
==0003==
46:- **Block base type is `RefCounted`**, never `Resource` (a `.tres` can embed scripts; Save/Load SL-2) or `Node` (kernel H10).
53:- **Kernel H1.** The kernel's members are an allow-listed set (`kernel.clock`, the queue, the registries, the binding tables, the command log, kernel state, diagnostics); an acceptance criterion lints it.
235:**Violations** are counted diagnostics, not fault codes, and never change kernel state unless the GDD says so. Closed set: `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`, `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED`, `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE`, `CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`, `CONTEXT_REENTRY`, `SUBMIT_DURING_SAVING`, `HANDLE_UNREGISTERED`, `RESULT_HANDLER_DEAD`, `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER`, `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT`, `KNOB_REFUSED`, `BINDING_DRIFT`, `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED`, `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` (a boot warning). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` each also calls `violation_handler(code, detail)`.
243:`ReadViews` has two faces, issued as facets by the composition root (ADR-0001): **`SimViews`** (to `validate`, `apply` and hooks) and **`PresentationViews`** (to subscribers). Both have `get(block_id: StringName) -> Object`, returning the owner's facade, which the caller casts to the owner's view class. For a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, `SimViews.get` returns that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation; `PresentationViews` returns the real facade. A fault in `read_view` or `empty_view` at the freeze is recorded and leaves the empty view in place; it never faults the kernel (CR-19(a)). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` hashes SIM blocks per dispatch batch and around P5 (`TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` 1.0 ms, full sweep every `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` 60), which catches a facade that leaks a mutable reference.
268:### 10. Kernel members (the H1 allow-list)
270:Everything this ADR adds to the kernel lives under the GDD's allow-listed groups, so the H1 lint stays a fixed list: **registries** (descriptors, the compiled schedule, the fault-domain table, `registry_valid`, the transition table); **kernel_state** (current state, the `PRIOR` return state, the reused contexts, tokens and scope objects); **diagnostics** (violation counters, boot warnings, the fault log).
395:- **Cons**: Violates H10; registration would depend on tree order rather than an explicit declaration (CR-6).

content.thinking:
I'm noticing ADR-0003's claim that PresentationViews returns the real facade for PERCEPTION_OUT blocks conflicts with ADR-0009 §1's rule that the default PresentationFacet returns an empty view — this falls under R13 as an ADR-0003 vs ADR-0009 conflict, separate from ADR-0004's main focus. I'm also starting to look at ADR-0003's SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE hashing mechanism.

Checking whether ADR-0004's audit timing right before P5 aligns with the tripwire's sweep budget — it seems the audit samples rather than fully sweeps, which is consistent. Then I'm examining whether has_opened from ADR-0005 stays true after P4 closes, since that ambiguity matters for whether the audit correctly catches BLOCK_HASH_IN_WRITE on touched blocks; I'd flag this as a minor cross-ADR clarification for ADR-0005 to define "active" as any non-CLOSED phase, though the audit might bypass block_hash entirely via an internal kernel path.

Looking deeper, the audit's reliance on "no key marked in that interval" over a 60-tick dev sweep window seems weak since unrelated marks could occur, but that's acknowledged as sampling. There's also an unspecified but trivial requirement to track a per-block flag for whether any key was marked since the last sweep.

Now I'm turning to internal issues in ADR-0004 itself — first, whether a pooled NotifyEvent retained by a subscriber beyond batch poisoning is a problem (minor), and second, whether MAX_EVENTS_PER_FRAME is scoped per-block or globally, which is ambiguous given each block seems to have its own event lists for tick and frame.

Following that, I note more ambiguity around whether per-block event lists need preallocated capacity when folding tick events into the frame list, which is another minor finding. Then I'm checking that per-tick event delivery happens correctly before the fold, that the KeyBuf swap properly re-points the ChangeBatch facade afterward, and that the DirtyAccumulator's union-beyond-capacity merge cost is acceptable at O(65k) worst-case for 256 keys. Finally, I spot a real inconsistency: lowering the MAX_DIRTY_KEYS knob at runtime wouldn't actually shrink the KeyBuf's effective capacity since `mark` checks against the buffer's fixed size rather than the current knob value, so the lowered limit needs to be represented separately.

This should be fixed by latching a separate capacity field at P0 rather than relying on the buffer's raw size, since the DirtyAccumulator's capacity is also tied to a sized field that could diverge from the knob if lowered — causing merged and per-tick collapse behavior to disagree, which would break the validation test expecting a knob change during one tick to take effect by the next tick. I verify that the "257th key triggers ALL" logic is otherwise correct under the current size-based check, and that subscription re-checks at freeze time are fine since Godot's ObjectID validator prevents instance ID reuse issues. I'm now about to look at who controls the class gate.

Looking closer, I spot a real conflict: ADR-0009 says the composition root chooses the class at facet issue, with PresentationFacet forwarding it, but ADR-0004 shows NotifyFacet.subscribe taking a raw class parameter that lets any holder subscribe as any class except gated ones — and the diagrams in the two ADRs disagree about what presentation actually receives, while ADR-0010's facet list omits both NotifyFacet and PresentationFacet entirely. I think the fix is to make NotifyFacet composition-root-only or bind the class at issue time, with presentation instead using ADR-0009's wrapped PresentationFacet. I also flag that NotifyContext's naming clashes with ARCH-08's `*Context` convention, suggesting ADR-0010 should narrow ARCH-08 to cover only tick-phase contexts.

I'm sorting out where types like DirtyAccumulator should live given their dependency on KeyBuf in kernel core, leaning toward either moving KeyBuf to shared or keeping DirtyAccumulator self-contained in facets, with ADR-0010 owning the placement rule and ADR-0004 adding a line about it since its current "Subscriber side" comment for NotifyFacet seems inaccurate. Next I want to check the registry's architecture.yaml for relevant stances — things like presentation_submit_without_handle, owner_callable_contract, block_registration, frame_order, and fault_domain_table — then grep the TR baseline for ADR-0004 references and verify how ADR-0010's "Enables" list cross-references ADR-0004.

Looking closer, I'm untangling a circular Enables relationship between ADR-0010 and ADR-0004: since ADR-0010 is the lint mechanism and ADR-0004 just adds a rule slot to it, I think ADR-0010 should be upstream with ADR-0004 depending on it softly rather than listing it under Enables, while confirming the symmetric ADR-0005/ADR-0004 relationship is already correct and noting that ADR-0009's Depends On list is missing ADR-0004 as a fix needed there.

Now I'm checking whether ADR-0004 should Enable ADR-0006 based on whether OQ-F gets answered by the control-plane end-of-tick callback, and confirming ADR-0004's relationship to ADR-0007 and ADR-0001 look fine as-is. Next I want to verify KRN-LAT-02's coverage in the Spikes section against what ADR-0009 claims about it, then move into right-sizing checks for replication classes, diagnostic wildcards, event pools, and audit/touch serial fields.

For the audit mechanism specifically, I'm noting that most large blocks are quiet (Graph, Emitter, Body, Suit, Controller, Sanity), so the hash audit really only covers Layout, Web, and Attention — moderate value for modest cost (a per-block flag plus a compare). This feels like something that could reasonably be scoped down to tests-only at MVP rather than sampled in dev builds, which I'll flag as a minor right-sizing suggestion.

There's also a consistency issue: the audit hash depends on SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE, which per ADR-0004 only runs under STRICT_DEBUG, yet the ADR says the tripwire should cover dev, playtest, and test builds. If STRICT_DEBUG is off during playtest, the tripwire won't run, so the audit has nothing to reuse — meaning the audit's build coverage needs to exactly match the tripwire's, which it currently doesn't.

On determinism, delivery order follows registration order and depends on composition root setup, which seems fine; but the deferred-application approach of rebuilding per-block subscriber arrays only when pending introduces allocation that needs to be checked against the no-allocation-in-quiet-blocks rule.

A pending prune of a dead subscriber during a quiet tick would allocate, slightly violating that same rule, though it's a minor issue since quiet ticks aren't steady-state — fixed in-place arrays would avoid it. Dead subscriber detection via is_valid() checked right before invocation seems fine, though it only catches staleness when the block is actually dirty.

I'm also flagging that get_argument_count() on Callable was only added in Godot 4.3, and the earlier probe list didn't check for it — worth adding to the probe, though is_standard() has been around since 4.0 so that's fine. Finally, looking at how the typed dictionary caches a block index for dirty-mark comparisons — since StringName comparison is just a pointer compare, that lookup should be cheap and isn't a concern.

For restore semantics, deliver_all pushing every subscription across both PER_TICK and FRAME_MERGED classes at the restored tick looks correct. I'm now weighing whether ADR-0004 could add a lightweight `is_load` flag to ChangeBatch to satisfy ADR-0009's restore-marker need without touching ADR-0001, but recognizing that ADR-0009 needs this signal at the driver level before present, not scoped to individual handlers — so a per-presenter batch flag doesn't naturally propagate to a global driver check, which suggests the clock-field approach ADR-0009 prefers is actually the more sensible one.

For R12's Save/Load trigger, I'm noting a gap: ADR-0004 wants to poll a read view, ADR-0006 treats Save/Load as a control-plane caller polling at priority 0, but neither addresses how POD_ARRIVED/BERTHED events (not persistent state) get observed through polling alone. My recommendation is that the Web Map ADR should expose monotonic counters like last_pod_arrived_T and last_berthed_T so Save/Load can poll those directly, and ADR-0004 should settle OQ-3 by stating there's no control-plane callback and dropping Alternative 9 rather than leaving it open.

For R13, I'm confirming it — ADR-0004 §6 delegates the subscribe check and ADR-0009 doesn't restrict it further, though ADR-0003 conflicts by having PresentationViews return a real facade for PERCEPTION_OUT. The deeper issue is whether the subscribe-time restriction is even necessary: dirty keys for perception data could leak "something changed" signals, potentially exposing the existence of hallucinations to subscribers without perception access. I'm concluding a subscribe-time check is cheap and worth keeping, with ADR-0004 owning the mechanism (the gate itself) and ADR-0009 owning the policy of which facets get perception access.

For R14, I'm confirming that ADR-0004's acceptance is gated on ADR-0001/0003 amendments — the ordering note needs to explicitly say acceptance requires those ADRs accepted "with the cross-ADR amendments applied." Since ADR-0004 can't truly be accepted while ADR-0003's audit description still lacks emit_event, I'm treating this as a blocking finding, though the actual fix belongs to ADR-0001/0003 as the owning amendments.

For R15, I'm checking whether ADR-0004 actually documents its registry candidates. It references fault_domain_table as "extended by this ADR's candidates" and the review log claims they're unchanged from original authoring, but there's no actual section listing them anywhere in the doc. That's a gap worth flagging — the ADR needs a dedicated Registry Candidates section enumerating things like notify_transport, block_registration signature, state_ownership touch_serial, and the forbidden pattern entries.

docs/architecture/adr-0003-state-block-registry-and-owner-contract.md:188:**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3). **Fail-closed never depends on an engine error aborting the callee** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review)*: a release build may log a script error and continue. It is carried by the explicit paths only — mutator status checks, `scope.fault` and the closed scope — with the `STRICT_DEBUG` checks and ADR-0004's debug-build missed-mark hash as backstops. An engine error that a release build swallows and that no mutator detects is outside what the kernel can see; KRN-CTX-06 documents it rather than claims it.
design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md:137:**Read views are getter-only facades or copies, and the guarantee is 'structural plus tripwire'** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. GDScript has no const references: a `Dictionary`, `Array` or Packed array returned from a view is a live container any reader could write to. A read view therefore returns either a facade exposing getters only (indexed access into the owner's storage, for large blocks such as the Graph) or a copy (`duplicate_deep()` / `duplicate()`, for small blocks) — never the owner's live container. What the kernel enforces *structurally* is the issuance surface: `WriteScope` exists only in P2/P3, `PRESENTATION` and `PROJECTOR` receive no submit handle, and owners register no subscription. What it can only *detect* is a reader that mutates a container it should not hold: under `STRICT_DEBUG` the kernel hashes the `SIM` blocks (uncached, so a write that bypassed the dirty bit is seen) **once per dispatch batch** (before the batch's first `validate` and after its last — a `validate` that mutated is caught as a changed hash across the batch and named by block, which is coarser than per-command and is the cost trade) **and once around P5**, and a changed hash is a `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` violation naming the block *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the earlier "around each `validate`" cost up to 129 uncached encodes per tick and made the dev profile unplayable during a burst)*. The tripwire is the only detector for a missed dirty mark, so its **coverage may not shrink**: these per-tick hashes run under a wall-clock budget cap (`TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS`, dev only, **[PLACEHOLDER]** 1.0 ms per tick; blocks over the cap are deferred, never skipped), and **every `SIM` block is swept at least once every `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` ticks (**[PLACEHOLDER]** 60) wherever the budget deferred it**; the test profile ignores the budget and always hashes uncached around every batch and P5 *(CD resolution of the tripwire disagreement)*. H3/H4 are thus enforced by structure, lint and tripwire together, not by structure alone.
design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md:155:- **(d) Violations.** A *violation* (write outside a `WriteScope`, a sim read of `PERCEPTION_OUT`, a hook reaching the `PLAYER` ingress, a submit during `SAVING`, a payload that passed the size check but fails the round-trip, a `SIM` hash change at the tripwire) is, in every build: the offending action refused, a named diagnostics counter incremented, `push_error` called. Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the kernel additionally calls the injected `violation_handler(code, detail)`; the dev default halts via `assert(false)`, the test default records. No state-machine outcome (`FAULTED`, reject reasons, results) differs between profiles.
design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md:156:- **(e) KernelProfile.** `KernelProfile` ∈ {`STRICT_DEBUG`, `LENIENT_RELEASE`} is injected at construction (H10) and never read from `OS.is_debug_build()` inside the kernel, so one test process can construct a kernel per profile and exercise both branches. `STRICT_DEBUG` enables only the extras: the per-command serialization round-trip (CR-4), the violation handler, the `SIM` tripwire (CR-12) and the counter test seams.
design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md:680:- **If `validate` reports a fault, returns without the sentinel, calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()`, or has a side effect**: a reported fault, a missing sentinel or a missing outcome is a defect and moves the kernel to `FAULTED` exactly as an apply fault (the command receives `Faulted(code)`, with `INCOMPLETE` or `NO_OUTCOME`); it is not a rejection. Side effects in `validate` are not detectable at run time by the kernel in release; under `STRICT_DEBUG` the `SIM` hash tripwire (CR-12) detects them, and in all builds they are a lint/test obligation on the owner. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

findings.text: Two parts of the spec disagree with each other about the dirty-key knob. § 3 lets MAX_DIRTY_KEYS be lowered at run time, taking effect at the next tick's P0, and Validation Criteria line 502 tests that. But KeyBuf.mark (§ 4) collapses when `count == buf.size()`, and buf.size() is the capacity fixed at the freeze, which never changes. DirtyAccumulator is also sized from the freeze value (NotifyFacet.key_capacity). As written, lowering the knob has no effect, and the acceptance test cannot pass. The fold union in § 6 has the same problem.
findings.amendment: § 4: add `var cap: int` to KeyBuf, separate from buf.size(). Set it with `set_cap(k)` on every tick and frame buffer at the P0 latch, and test `count == cap` in mark() and in the § 6 union. § 5: say that DirtyAccumulator collapses at the latched cap, exposed as `NotifyFacet.key_cap()` read at absorb time, or say explicitly that it keeps the sized capacity and why that is acceptable. Alternatively, make the knob Boot-only and record this as a deviation from D.9 under GDD sync.

findings.text: Accepting this ADR depends on amendments to ADR-0001 and ADR-0003 that have not been made. A grep of ADR-0001, 0002 and 0003 finds none of these: deliver_frame_end, NotifyFacet, register_key_space, emit_event, SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED, DIRTY_KEY_INVALID, touch_serial, MISSED_DIRTY_MARK, EVENT_OVERFLOW. ADR-0003 line 179 still states the literal rule this ADR replaces in § 7 ('hash each block before and after a tick and compare with whether it was marked'). ADR-0003 line 235 still has a closed violation set without the five new names, and its § 10 H1 allow-list has no touch serial. The Ordering Note only requires those ADRs to be Accepted, not amended.

findings.text: The ADR never says where its public types live in the source tree, and the way it describes NotifyFacet conflicts with ADR-0009. Under ADR-0010 ARCH-08 (§ 2.2 rule 4, line 165), presentation may not name any `*Context`, and the kernel/facets list (line 124) has only ChangeBatch. This ADR requires every handler to take a NotifyContext and return a CompletionToken, so every presenter would fail the lint (R1). Separately, § 2 and the diagram hand NotifyFacet, with a free `cls: int` argument, straight to presentation `setup()`. ADR-0009 § 1 says the composition root fixes the class when it issues the facet, and presenters receive a PresentationFacet with `subscribe(block_id, handler, name)`. As written, any holder of NotifyFacet can pick its own class. DirtyAccumulator 'uses the same KeyBuf code as § 4', which ties a presentation-side type to kernel-core code.

Make DirtyAccumulator self-contained, or move KeyBuf to `src/shared/`. In kernel core: KeyBuf (if not shared), the registry and KeySpaceDescriptor, reached by owners through BlockRegistrar. findings.text: The § 7 quiet-block list is inconsistent with the ADR's own examples. § 7 cites Web Map WM-2 ('zero keys per tick during a leg') as a reason the literal audit is wrong, and TR-webmap-024 and ADR-0005 § 5.2 say the same. A non-quiet web.state that writes leg progress would raise MISSED_DIRTY_MARK on every sweep.

findings.text: OQ-3 (Save/Load trigger path) is left open, and the open question loops between two ADRs (R12). ADR-0004 points to ADR-0006, and ADR-0006 OQ-F points back to ADR-0004. ADR-0006 § 1.12's facet read list has no `web.state` entry, so the POD_ARRIVED and BERTHED autosave triggers in TR-webmap-023 currently have no path at all. findings.amendment: ADR-0004 owns the classes and events, so it should decide: reject Alternative 9 outright (no sixth class) and add no control-plane end-of-tick callback. Save/Load polls monotonic counters in owner read views (for example `web.view.pod_arrived_seq`/`last_pod_arrived_T` and `berthed_seq`), which cannot be lost to frame merging. Record the counters as a requirement on the Web Map ADR. ADR-0006 adds web.state to its § 1.12 read list and closes OQ-F. Re-tag TR-webmap-023's Save/Load half to ADR-0006.

findings.text: There is no gate on subscribing to a PERCEPTION_OUT block (R13). The subscribe-time checks live in § 2 (checks 1 to 5) of this ADR, but § 6 and OQ-7 hand the PERCEPTION_OUT filter to ADR-0009 or ADR-0024. ADR-0009 only blocks reads (`empty_view`), so any PRESENTATION subscriber can still subscribe to `sanity.perception` and learn its dirty-key ids, which leaks the timing and identity of perception changes. ADR-0003 § 7 (line 243) says PresentationViews returns the *real* facade for PERCEPTION_OUT, which contradicts ADR-0009 § 1.

ADR-0009 decides which facets carry that flag, and ADR-0003 § 7 is amended to the two-face rule. Add a Validation line for it and close OQ-7.

findings.text: The dependency tables are not symmetric (R18). ADR-0004 and ADR-0010 each list the other under Enables. ADR-0004 actually consumes ADR-0010: it names `src/kernel/` and `src/presentation/` paths and relies on SIM-13 and ARCH-08. findings.text: One engine API rests on training knowledge only. Subscribe check 1 uses `Callable.get_argument_count()`, which is not among probes (a) to (f). The other Callable methods were probed.
findings.amendment: Either add get_argument_count() on a method Callable, a lambda and a `.bind()` result to the probe list (one more headless run), or mark it UNVERIFIED in Engine Compatibility with KRN-LAT-02 as the settling spike.

findings.text: Right-sizing and a consistency nit. (a) The 60-tick sampled audit in dev and playtest builds adds little over the every-tick test audit, because the quiet blocks (the large ones) are excluded, and under STRICT_DEBUG the dev default halts on a violation. For a solo MVP, the test-profile audit plus the per-mutator exact-key tests is enough. The same reasoning applies to both. (c) A load-time is_all batch cannot be told apart from an overflow is_all. ADR-0009 works around this with a new PresentationClock.load_seq (N2).

findings.text: Two parts of the spec disagree with each other about the dirty-key knob. § 3 lets MAX_DIRTY_KEYS be lowered at run time, taking effect at the next tick's P0, and Validation Criteria line 502 tests that. But KeyBuf.mark (§ 4) collapses when `count == buf.size()`, and buf.size() is the capacity fixed at the freeze, which never changes. DirtyAccumulator is also sized from the freeze value (NotifyFacet.key_capacity). As written, lowering the knob has no effect, and the acceptance test cannot pass. The fold union in § 6 has the same problem.
findings.amendment: § 4: add `var cap: int` to KeyBuf, separate from buf.size(). Set it with `set_cap(k)` on every tick and frame buffer at the P0 latch, and test `count == cap` in mark() and in the § 6 union. § 5: say that DirtyAccumulator collapses at the latched cap, exposed as `NotifyFacet.key_cap()` read at absorb time, or say explicitly that it keeps the sized capacity and why that is acceptable. Alternatively, make the knob Boot-only and record this as a deviation from D.9 under GDD sync.

findings.text: Accepting this ADR depends on amendments to ADR-0001 and ADR-0003 that have not been made. A grep of ADR-0001, 0002 and 0003 finds none of these: deliver_frame_end, NotifyFacet, register_key_space, emit_event, SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED, DIRTY_KEY_INVALID, touch_serial, MISSED_DIRTY_MARK, EVENT_OVERFLOW. ADR-0003 line 179 still states the literal rule this ADR replaces in § 7 ('hash each block before and after a tick and compare with whether it was marked'). ADR-0003 line 235 still has a closed violation set without the five new names, and its § 10 H1 allow-list has no touch serial. The Ordering Note only requires those ADRs to be Accepted, not amended.

findings.text: The ADR never says where its public types live in the source tree, and the way it describes NotifyFacet conflicts with ADR-0009. Under ADR-0010 ARCH-08 (§ 2.2 rule 4, line 165), presentation may not name any `*Context`, and the kernel/facets list (line 124) has only ChangeBatch. This ADR requires every handler to take a NotifyContext and return a CompletionToken, so every presenter would fail the lint (R1). Separately, § 2 and the diagram hand NotifyFacet, with a free `cls: int` argument, straight to presentation `setup()`. ADR-0009 § 1 says the composition root fixes the class when it issues the facet, and presenters receive a PresentationFacet with `subscribe(block_id, handler, name)`. State that NotifyFacet is held only by the composition root and that its class is fixed when it is issued (for example `NotifyFacet.for_class(cls)` returns a class-bound facet). Presentation receives ADR-0009's PresentationFacet. Change the 'Subscriber side (src/presentation/...)' comment to match. ADR-0010 then narrows ARCH-08 (see R1).

findings.text: OQ-5 and the conditional D.12 sync are already settled. ADR-0005 § 5.1 and § 5.2 adopt the touch serial as the cache validity input, and ADR-0005's Depends On cites ADR-0004 for it. ADR-0005's 'fallback if the serial does not survive the joint review' no longer applies.

findings.text: The audit's build gating does not match the tripwire it reuses, and the hash path it relies on is unclear. § 7 says the audit runs in 'dev, playtest and test builds' and reuses the SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE hashes. The tripwire runs only under the injected `STRICT_DEBUG` KernelProfile (kernel GDD CR-19(e), ADR-0003 line 243), and nothing read says whether playtest builds run STRICT_DEBUG (UNVERIFIED). findings.text: Two zero-allocation claims rest on structures the ADR never specifies. (a) § 6 gives each block 'an event list' per buffer, while § 5 and Performance describe one preallocated pool. (b) § 2's deferred rebuild of per-block subscriber arrays 'when a request is pending' can fall on a quiet-tick boundary, which Implementation Guidelines say must never allocate. The case is a DEAD_SUBSCRIBER prune.

Alternatively, exempt the rebuild explicitly from the zero-allocation rule as bounded and outside steady state, and say so in KRN-PERF-01. Poison pooled NotifyEvents together with the batch under STRICT_DEBUG.

This ADR requires every handler to take a NotifyContext and return a CompletionToken, so every presenter would fail the lint (R1). Separately, § 2 and the diagram hand NotifyFacet, with a free `cls: int` argument, straight to presentation `setup()`. ADR-0009 § 1 says the composition root fixes the class when it issues the facet, and presenters receive a PresentationFacet with `subscribe(block_id, handler, name)`. As written, any holder of NotifyFacet can pick its own class. DirtyAccumulator 'uses the same KeyBuf code as § 4', which ties a presentation-side type to kernel-core code.

State that NotifyFacet is held only by the composition root and that its class is fixed when it is issued (for example `NotifyFacet.for_class(cls)` returns a class-bound facet). Presentation receives ADR-0009's PresentationFacet. Change the 'Subscriber side (src/presentation/...)' comment to match. ADR-0010 then narrows ARCH-08 (see R1).

findings.text: OQ-5 and the conditional D.12 sync are already settled. ADR-0005 § 5.1 and § 5.2 adopt the touch serial as the cache validity input, and ADR-0005's Depends On cites ADR-0004 for it. ADR-0005's 'fallback if the serial does not survive the joint review' no longer applies.

The tripwire runs only under the injected `STRICT_DEBUG` KernelProfile (kernel GDD CR-19(e), ADR-0003 line 243), and nothing read says whether playtest builds run STRICT_DEBUG (UNVERIFIED). Also, ADR-0005 § 5.3 check (2) makes the public `block_hash` return BLOCK_HASH_IN_WRITE for any block the active scope has opened 'until the scope is re-armed'. If the around-P5 tripwire calls the public API after P4, it would refuse exactly the touched blocks the audit needs.

findings.text: Two zero-allocation claims rest on structures the ADR never specifies. (a) § 6 gives each block 'an event list' per buffer, while § 5 and Performance describe one preallocated pool. It does not say whether MAX_EVENTS_PER_TICK 64 is global or per block, or what container the per-block lists are. A growable Array would allocate on append. (b) § 2's deferred rebuild of per-block subscriber arrays 'when a request is pending' can fall on a quiet-tick boundary, which Implementation Guidelines say must never allocate. The case is a DEAD_SUBSCRIBER prune.
findings.amendment: State that the 64 per tick and MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME x 64 per frame limits are global. Per-block event lists should be fixed-size `PackedInt32Array` index lists into the global pool, preallocated at the freeze. Per-block subscriber lists should be fixed-capacity (MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS) packed index arrays rebuilt in place. Alternatively, exempt the rebuild explicitly from the zero-allocation rule as bounded and outside steady state, and say so in KRN-PERF-01. Poison pooled NotifyEvents together with the batch under STRICT_DEBUG.

findings.text: The § 7 quiet-block list is inconsistent with the ADR's own examples. § 7 cites Web Map WM-2 ('zero keys per tick during a leg') as a reason the literal audit is wrong, and TR-webmap-024 and ADR-0005 § 5.2 say the same. Yet web.state is missing from the quiet list (Graph, Emitter, Body, Suit, Controller, Sanity). Attention (TR-attention-026, polled every frame) may also write without keys. A non-quiet web.state that writes leg progress would raise MISSED_DIRTY_MARK on every sweep.
findings.amendment: Say the list is illustrative. Make each owner's KeySpaceDescriptor plus the per-owner key-space CI test the normative source. Add web.state as quiet, unless the Web Map ADR guarantees no write without a key during a leg, and flag attention.state for its owner's ADR to decide.

For a solo MVP, the test-profile audit plus the per-mutator exact-key tests is enough.
